items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Kenny’s girlfriend at the time was a bassist named Tracy Wormworth who played with the B-52s. ... Her sister Mary Wormworth lived two doors down from me at Berklee... I said, 'Call him right now.' So she calls him.

ctx.x: Would you talk a little bit more about Kenny? What were some of the things you enjoyed, and inspired you in his playing?

I think that… the first thing is that his sound on the piano was just unbelievable. And I grew up with a man who had that sound when he played – although not that style. The modern jazz sound is a much lighter sound. I don’t prefer it. I prefer density in the tone. And Kenny just had that in spades and it was…Soon as I heard it I said, “Aw, man, this is the guy. And, ah… I remember when I….He had all these…They used to call him “the phantom,” because he couldn’t say no to anybody. So if you ask him to do…
